los.text: Demonstrate a comprehensive physical examination of the shoulder.
los.html:
• Look, feel, move, special tests (compare with the other side; expose both shoulders).
StepDetail
LookFrom front, side, back: wasting (deltoid, supraspinatus, infraspinatus), asymmetry, scars, swelling, winging of the scapula
FeelTemperature, then bony landmarks: sternoclavicular joint, clavicle, ACJ, acromion, spine of scapula, humeral head; muscles
Move (active then passive)
  • Flexion 180°
  • Extension 60°
  • Abduction 180° (painful arc 60–120°: impingement)
  • Adduction
  • External rotation (lost early in frozen shoulder)
  • Internal rotation (hand behind back)
FunctionHands behind head and behind back
Special testTests
Empty can (Jobe's)Supraspinatus
External rotation against resistanceInfraspinatus, teres minor
Gerber's lift-off / belly pressSubscapularis
Hawkins–KennedyImpingement
Scarf testACJ
Apprehension testAnterior instability
  • Finish: examine the neck and the elbow (referred pain), neurovascular check (axillary nerve: "regimental badge" sensation).

los.text: Understand the principles of prescribing from a legal and clinical perspective
los.html:
Legal
  • Prescribing is restricted by law (Human Medicines Regulations 2012)
  • POMs need a registered prescriber
  • Controlled drugs (Misuse of Drugs Regulations 2001) need extra details and safe custody
  • Prescribers are personally accountable.
ClinicalIndication, evidence, contraindications, interactions, dose for the patient (age, weight, renal/hepatic function), monitoring, review date; involve the patient and document.
Errors to avoidAbbreviations (write "units" and "micrograms" in full), trailing zeros ("5 mg" not "5.0 mg"), missing allergy status, illegible writing.

los.text: Record patient observations accurately and in accordance with clinical guidelines
los.html:
ObservationHowNormal adult
Respiratory rateCount 60 s12–20
Oxygen saturationPulse oximeter, note air or oxygen94–98% (88–92% if hypercapnic risk)
Blood pressureCorrect cuff, arm at heart levelSystolic 111–219 scores 0
PulseRadial, 60 s51–90
ConsciousnessACVPUAlert
TemperatureTympanic or oral36.1–38.0 °C
  • Record accurately at the time, in the right place, and escalate abnormal values.

los.text: Complete a NEWS chart with accurate clinical data and interpret scores appropriately
los.html:
ScoreNEWS2 parameter thresholds (score 3)
RR≤8 or ≥25
SpO₂ (scale 1)≤91%
On oxygenAdds 2
Systolic BP≤90 or ≥220
Pulse≤40 or ≥131
ConsciousnessNew confusion, V, P or U
Temperature≤35.0 °C
Total NEWS2Response
0–4Ward-based care; 4–6-hourly obs (12-hourly if 0)
3 in any single parameterUrgent ward review
5–6Urgent response: doctor review, consider critical care; hourly obs
≥7Emergency response: senior/critical care team, continuous monitoring
  • Use SpO₂ scale 2 (target 88–92%) only for confirmed hypercapnic respiratory failure.

los.text: Differentiate between subjective and objective information when obtaining a patient history
los.html:
SubjectiveObjective
WhatWhat the patient reports (symptoms, feelings, history)What can be observed or measured (signs, observations, results)
Example"I feel short of breath"RR 28, SpO₂ 90%, crackles
Where in notesHistory (SOAP: S)Examination and investigations (SOAP: O)
  • SOAP notes: Subjective, Objective, Assessment, Plan.

los.text: Organise and present clinical findings in a structured and logical format
los.html:
PresentIdentifying details, presenting complaint, HPC (key positives and negatives), relevant PMH, drugs and allergies, social, family, ICE, then summary, differential and plan.
Keep it focusedLead with what matters; finish with a one-line summary.

los.text: Interpret a patient's perspective on their current condition
los.html:
Explore"What do you think is going on?", "What do you understand about your condition?"
WhyBeliefs shape worries and adherence; correcting misunderstandings builds trust.
RespondAcknowledge their view, explain the medical view in plain language, find common ground.

los.text: Identify and explore a patient's concerns during consultation
los.html:
Ask directly"Is there anything in particular that's worrying you?", "What's your biggest concern?"
Pick up cuesHesitation, repeated mentions, body language.
Respond with empathy and address the concern specifically (don't just reassure).

los.text: Clarify a patient’s expectations from the consultation to guide shared decision making
los.html:
Ask"What were you hoping we could do for you today?", "What would you like to happen?"
Why
  • Unmet expectations (e.g. antibiotics, scan, sick note) lead to dissatisfaction
  • Clarifying them allows shared decision making: explain options, benefits and risks, agree a plan together.
